note: These scenarios run in your browser against an in-memory model of UniFest's rules: the allowed values, unique keys and delete rules in its MySQL schema export, and the dashboard's role checks. They do not connect to the real system or its data.

scenarios.title: An admin can approve a pending event
steps: A student submits an event, which starts as 'pending'.
An admin approves it, setting the status to 'approved'.

scenarios.title: There is no 'rejected' status; rejected events are archived
steps: An event status is set to 'rejected'.
The workflow only defines pending, approved and archived, so Reject stores 'archived' instead.

scenarios.title: An event can be limited to university members
steps: An organiser sets an event's visibility to 'university', so only signed-in users can see it.

scenarios.title: An unsupported event mode is rejected
steps: An event's mode is set to 'Recorded', which is not one of Physical, Online or Hybrid.

scenarios.title: Two accounts cannot share an email
steps: An account exists for student@example.com.
Someone registers again with the same email.

scenarios.title: There is no separate organiser role
steps: A user's role is set to 'organizer'.
Roles are admin, staff, student and public; staff and students organise events with their normal role.

scenarios.title: The schema alone does not stop duplicate registrations
steps: User 3 is registered for event 1.
A second registration row for user 3 and event 1 is inserted.
There is no unique key on user and event, so the event page's check for an existing registration is what prevents this.

scenarios.title: Deleting an organiser removes their events
steps: A staff member has created events.
An admin deletes the staff member's account.

scenarios.title: An event with registrations cannot be deleted
steps: An event has registered participants.
The organiser deletes the event.
The registrations foreign key has no ON DELETE rule, so MySQL blocks the delete.

scenarios.title: Deleting an event removes its feedback
steps: An event has ratings and reviews.
The event is deleted.

scenarios.title: A public user cannot create events
steps: A public (guest) user opens the dashboard.

scenarios.title: A student can create events
steps: A student opens the dashboard.

scenarios.title: Only admins can manage users
steps: A staff member opens the dashboard.

scenarios.title: Every user sees the events they joined
steps: A public user who registered for an event opens the dashboard.
